title: Telemetry event schema v4 proposal
content:
Purpose:
This document proposes a v4 event schema (and a lightweight compatibility shim) for Redwood audit/telemetry exports. It focuses on: mapping events into SIEM/ECS, carrying RBAC v2 policy context for change events, enabling evidence automation for compliance evidence capture, and a pragmatic versioning + migration plan that minimizes downstream breakage.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goal: Single envelope format that is backwards-mappable from v1-v3 with minimal loss.
- Goal: Explicit fields for policy snapshots, evidence references, and redaction metadata.
- Goal: ECS-friendly mappings (ECS 1.13 baseline) to ease ingestion into customer SIEMs.
- Non-goal: Replace every product-specific event field. We expect product teams to continue emitting domain fields in a product_payload map.

Core design ideas (high level):
1) Event envelope + schema_version: every event MUST include a top-level "schema_version" and an "event_type". Major version changes are breaking; minor versions are additive.
2) Event shim: a lightweight "event_shim_v*N*" block allows us to carry legacy field mappings so older collectors can continue to interpret meaning. The shim is optional but recommended for server-to-server exports.
3) Actor normalization: normalize actor identities into an "actor" object with: id, principal_type (user/service/key), integrated_identity (okta/email/oidc sub), and actor_roles array (resolved at event time).
4) Resource lifecycle action: unify CRUD/update/permission-change into an "action" taxonomy (create, read, update, delete, grant, revoke, escalate, deescalate, login, logout, api_call).
5) Outcome and evidence: standardized outcome enum (success/failure/partial) plus an "outcome_code" for machine classifications; evidence array with signed artifact refs (S3 keys, KMS-backed URIs) for automated evidence retrieval.

Proposed canonical field list (v4 envelope) -- text description, not prescriptive ordering:
- schema_version: "4.0"
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_id: UUIDv4 (preferably request scoped)
- event_type: short token (e.g., "model.deploy", "policy.change", "auth.token.issue")
- request_id: optional request-scoped id (helps correlate multi-stage requests)
- correlation_id: optional cross-service id
- actor: stringified summary (id) plus actor_attributes in product_payload (see actor_fields below)
- actor_fields: list of normalized actor properties: id, principal_type, integ_identity, actor_roles, org_id, agent_version
- action: taxonomy token from canonical list (see above)
- resource: resource_type and resource_id token(s) (e.g., "dedicated_pool:pool-123")
- resource_meta: small map of resource-level attributes (size_hint, region, model_family) -- high cardinality caution
- outcome / outcome_code: outcome textual + numeric code for automated queries
- duration_ms: optional latency/duration
- geo: optional geo hint (region datacenter id only; PII redaction rules apply)
- product_payload: free-form product-specific fields (string map)
- evidence: array of artifact references (signed URI | s3://key | gs://) with mime, size_bytes, digest_sha256, access_control_snapshot
- policy_snapshot: present for policy change events or where relevant; a short hash + storage_ref to full policy blob; include minimal diffs when feasible
- redaction_version / pii_masked: explicit marker if payload had PII masked or tokens redacted, include redaction_policy_id
- retention_ttl_days: optional hint for downstream exporters
- tags: array of short strings for quick classification
- event_shim_v<N>: optional legacy mapping block to hold field translations for older parsers

Example event (as text sample):
{
  "schema_version": "4.0",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-02-12T17:23:04.123Z",
  "event_id": "b3d9f6a8-2c4d-4f7b-b1c1-0a9a5c6e8f2d",
  "event_type": "policy.change",
  "actor": "user:anika@redwood.ai",
  "actor_fields": "id=anika@redwood.ai;principal_type=user;actor_roles=security-admin,infra-auditor;org_id=rdw:org-42",
  "action": "grant",
  "resource": "rbac-policy:policy-72",
  "policy_snapshot": "s3://redwood-audit/policy_snapshots/policy-72-20260212.json.gz#sha256=...",
  "outcome": "success",
  "evidence": "s3://redwood-audit/evidence/policy-72-change-20260212.json.gz",
  "redaction_version": "r2"
}

Note: actor_fields and product_payload are encoded as semicolon-delimited k=v pairs to limit JSON nesting in the primary envelope; exporter libraries will provide helpers to parse them into structured objects for downstream systems.

SIEM / ECS mapping guidance:
- Map timestamp_utc -> @timestamp (ECS).
- event_id -> event.id, event.type -> event.category or event.type depending on SIEM.
- actor.id -> user.name / user.id when principal_type=user; when service principal -> service.name/service.id.
- outcome/outcome_code -> event.outcome and event.outcome_reason (custom field).
- evidence references map to file.metadata.* or to http / url.original where applicable.
- policy_snapshot URL should be mapped to "file.hash.*" if available and to "url.original" for retrieval in SIEM consoles.

RBAC v2 specifics: what to include in audit events
- Policy deltas: when policy changed, include a short delta summary in the envelope (added=[role:perm], removed=[...]), but store full policy JSON in policy_snapshot (deduped in object store).
- Resolved roles: include resolved actor_roles at event time so post-hoc lookups are possible even if policy changes.
- Policy version id: include policy_version and policy_author for traceability.

Evidence automation considerations:
- Evidence artifacts MUST be signed URIs with limited TTL for automated retrieval by compliance tooling. Include access_control_snapshot (ACLs/policy ids) so auditors can validate who had access at event time.
- Consider storing a small binary delta (diff) rather than a full blob for large artifacts (model bundle diffs, policy changes).
- For high-frequency events (auth tokens, token use), store summarized evidence (token id + sample metadata) and spill full payloads only when an alert or request for evidence occurs to save storage.

Versioning + migration strategy:
1) Adopt MAJOR.MINOR (e.g., 4.0).
2) Backwards compatibility: collectors should accept events with schema_version <= supported_major if an event_shim_x mapping exists; otherwise they should fall back to field heuristics.
3) Forward compatibility: do not reject unknown fields; log them and optionally surface telemetry about unexpected keys.
4) Migration path from v1-v3: provide a conversion library (Python/Go/Node) and a server-side conversion shim that can be deployed in the export pipeline to emit v4 while preserving an event_shim_v3 block for customers still on older ingestion rules.
5) Deprecation timeline: aim for 12 months from v4 GA to enforce removal of v1 parsing in Redwood-managed exporters; provide a paid extended support window for enterprise customers who need more time.

Operational notes / high-cardinality cautions:
- resource_meta and product_payload are common high-cardinality sources. Encourage product teams to only put tags and low-cardinality labels in the top-level tags field; put voluminous or high-card fields in product_payload with clear guidance.
- Evidence artifacts and policy_snapshot references should be deduplicated and stored with content-addressed keys (sha256) to reduce duplication costs.
- Add sampling knobs for non-critical telemetry (e.g., background health pings) to reduce ingestion costs to SIEMs.

Open questions and decision points (action items):
- Legal: recommended minimal retention for policy snapshots and evidence artifacts. (Owner: Legal, TODO: SEC-412).
- Redaction: standardize redaction_policy_id semantics to allow deterministic rehydration for auditors with proper keys. Decision due: 2026-03-15.
- High-frequency auth events: sample vs full storage policy (engineering to prototype memory/disk cost estimates).
- Shim adoption: which customer tiers get event_shim_v3 by default? (Recommend enterprise & dedicated customers; flag off for hosted free tier).

Appendix: migration checklist for product teams:
- Add schema_version and event_id to all emitted events.
- Resolve actor_roles at emission time for all auth/permission events.
- Start emitting policy_snapshot references for policy mutation events.
- Add redaction_version when any PII is removed.
- Coordinate with platform export team to turn on v4 conversion shim in staging; run ingest tests to customer SIEM (ECS mapping check).

Contact and review history:
- Drafted by: Anika Rao (security)
- Reviewers: Marco Diaz (infra), Jordan Lin (platform), Priya Patel (product security), Lina Gomez (compliance)
- Next review date: 2026-03-10 (notes: pushed to 2026-02-28 for engineering feedback)

This doc intentionally keeps examples concise; conversion utilities and schema reference (field-by-field formal spec) will be maintained in the linked Confluence page and the platform repo (see linked_artifacts).
